listening.general_standard: Can identify general information and specific details heard from short oral texts when spoken slowly and clearly.

specific_standards.receptive: Recognize the main ideas of longer conversational exchanges.
specific_standards.interactive: Respond to questions about requesting information.

learning_outcomes: Can recognize the main ideas in school news reports about community events (e.g., 'The school is organizing a clean-up day in the park next Saturday.' 'The class will visit Casco Viejo to learn about Panama's history.').

Can respond to simple questions when classmates ask for information about community events (e.g., 'Where is the school fair?' 'It's at the sports field.' 'When are the community's carnivals?' 'They are next year starting on February 14.' 'Where is the Fiestas Patrias parade?' 'It's on Central Avenue.').

Can identify specific details in conversations about local traditions and places (e.g., 'Our community is famous for its traditional dances.' 'In Panama, people celebrate the Desfile de las Mil Polleras in Las Tablas with colorful dresses and parades.').

reading.general_standard: Can interpret information in fictional and factual short texts using basic reading strategies such as skimming, scanning and making inferences.

specific_standards.reading_1: Identify specific information from fictional short texts.
specific_standards.reading_2: Identify the sequence of events in simple stories.
specific_standards.phonemic_awareness: Demonstrate knowledge of phonemic awareness by identifying short and long vowel sounds in orally stated single-syllable words.

learning_outcomes: Can identify specific information about community events in short fictional texts (e.g., 'The school organized a fair last week.' 'The community held a clean-up day at the park.').

Can recognize the sequence of events in simple stories about community traditions (e.g., Students read a story about the Desfile de las Mil Polleras and identify the order of events: 'First, the participants gathered, then the parade started, and finally, they celebrated with music and food.').

Can identify short and long vowel sounds in words related to community events (e.g., recognizing /æ/ in 'banner' vs. /eɪ/ in 'parade' or /ɪ/ in 'tradition' vs. /iː/ in 'queen' when reading about local celebrations).

speaking.general_standard: Can exchange information about a variety of familiar topics read and discussed in class.

specific_standards.productive: Describe others based on physical traits, personality, and type of relationship.
specific_standards.interactive: Exchange information on familiar topics with peers.

learning_outcomes: Can describe community members featured in local news using physical traits and personality adjectives (e.g., 'The reporter has short black hair and is very friendly.' 'The artisan is tall, wears a Sombrero Pintao, and is very proud of his work.').

Can ask and answer questions about community events and traditions with peers (e.g., 'What did you like about the Carnival in Penonomé?' 'I liked the queen's beautiful outfit and the music.' 'Did you go to the school fair?' 'Yes, I went with my friends.').
Can exchange information with peers about popular landmarks in their community (e.g., 'Isla Colón is a popular landmark in our province.' 'Yes, I went last month and saw a lot of tourists.').

writing.general_standard: Can create simple texts in various genres, such as narratives, plans, and descriptions, incorporating details and peer feedback to improve clarity.

specific_standards.productive: Write personal journal entries about daily experiences.
specific_standards.interactive: Write a short descriptive text about personal plans for various activities.

learning_outcomes: Can write personal journal entries describing recent community events they attended (e.g., 'Last weekend, I went to the Desfile de las Mil Polleras. I liked the colorful dresses and the music. It was really fun!').
Can write short descriptions of personal plans for upcoming community activities (e.g., 'Next month, I will visit Pedasi for Carnivals. I want to see the parade and the Carnival Queen's floats.').

Can create a simple community news report about a local event using descriptive adjectives (e.g., 'The school fair was last Friday. There were games, food stands, and music. Many students helped organize it, and everyone had fun.').

mediation.general_standard: Can use strategies such as simplifying instructions, explaining main ideas, and using visuals or examples to negotiate meanings with peers.

specific_standards.text_1: Write simple interpretations of common texts in English supported with visual aids.
specific_standards.text_2: Explain the main points of class readings to peers.

learning_outcomes: Can write simple summaries of community news articles with visual support (e.g., uses an image of the parade as an aid for the summary, 'The Desfile de las Mil Polleras took place last weekend. Many women wore colorful polleras and danced in the streets.').

Can explain the main points of class readings about Panamanian traditions using visuals (e.g., shows pictures of Carnival floats and attendees while explaining, 'The text talks about Carnival in Chitré. People enjoy the parades and music.').

Can simplify event flyers for peers, highlighting key details with visuals (e.g., 'The school fair is on Friday at 9 a.m.' with a drawing of a calendar and school, or 'The Fiestas Patrias parade starts at 10 a.m.' with a picture of a marching band).

recommended_grammatical_features: Past simple tense (e.g., 'The students prepared a mural about the Desfile de las Mil Polleras.' 'I visited the school fair last weekend.')
Compound sentences in the past tense with the conjunction 'but' (e.g., 'I liked the colorful floats during the Carnival parade, but I didn't like the loud music.')
Adjectives for describing physical appearance (e.g., 'Mr. Ricardo is tall and wears a sombrero pintao.')

pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness.pronunciation: Practice pronunciation of past tense -ed endings (/t/, /d/, /ɪd/) (e.g., /d/ in 'moved,' /t/ in 'liked,' /ɪd/ in 'wanted')
pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness.phonemic_awareness: Identifying short and long vowel sounds (e.g., recognizing /æ/ in 'banner' vs. /eɪ/ in 'parade' or /ɪ/ in 'tradition' vs. /iː/ in 'queen').

pragmatic_competences: Exchanging personal information: Can introduce themselves and share details about their community (e.g., 'I'm Julissa. I'm from Chitré, and I love the local festivals.')
Sharing past experiences and preferences: Can talk about past events and express likes or dislikes (e.g., 'I went to the Desfile de las Mil Polleras. I liked the different colorful polleras.')
Describing people and community members: Can describe community members using physical traits and personality (e.g., 'The artisan has curly hair and is very kind.')
communicative_competences.sociolinguistic_competences: Softening disagreement: Can express disagreement gently (e.g., 'I like parades, too, but I prefer to attend music shows during the festival.')

twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Students design a mural showcasing local traditions like Carnivals or Fiestas Patrias, adding captions with descriptive adjectives and past tense (e.g., 'The artisan wore a sombrero pintao.').

technology_integration: Multimedia Creation: Use digital tools to design community news reports, create visual murals, or produce video/audio recordings showcasing local events and traditions.
Collaborative Platforms: Utilize online platforms for group projects, enabling collaboration on writing, editing, and presenting community stories and interviews.

specific_standards.reading_1: Infer meaning from context clues in short texts.
specific_standards.reading_2: Write responses to questions about informational texts.
specific_standards.phonemic_awareness: Demonstrate knowledge of phonemic awareness by segmenting multisyllabic words into syllables.

learning_outcomes: Can infer meanings of environmental vocabulary from context (e.g., 'Go green means protecting nature.').
Can write reflections on environmental informative text by answering key questions and sharing their thoughts (e.g., 'What was the story about?' 'It was about saving water.').
Can segment multisyllabic words into syllables, demonstrating knowledge of phonemic awareness (e.g., dividing 'presentation' into 'pre-sen-ta-tion').

speaking.general_standard: Can exchange information about a variety of familiar topics read and discussed in class.

specific_standards.productive: Explain structured rules for specific activities, like playing a game, or collaborating on a project.
specific_standards.interactive: Coordinate roles and tasks for a group project.

learning_outcomes: Can explain rules for recycling (e.g., 'Everyone needs to bring their own bag.').
Can coordinate roles for the environmental project with classmates (e.g., 'You bring markers, and I'll bring paper.').
Can ask and answer logistics questions on recycling task (e.g., 'Do we wash bottles before putting them in recycling?').

writing.general_standard: Can create simple texts in various genres, such as narratives, plans, and descriptions, incorporating details and peer feedback to improve clarity.

specific_standards.productive: Draft descriptive texts about everyday events.
specific_standards.interactive: Write short scripts for plays collaboratively about familiar topics.

learning_outcomes: Can draft short scripts about everyday recycling activities (e.g., 'We wash the plastic and glass bottles every day.').
Can write descriptive texts on recycling projects (e.g., 'We collect the plastic bottles and sort them by color.').

Can collaborate with peers to write and perform short scripts about environmental projects (e.g., 'Let's write a play about how we recycle at school. I'll write the first part, and you can add the next part.').

mediation.general_standard: Can use strategies such as simplifying instructions, explaining main ideas, and using visuals or examples to negotiate meanings with peers.

specific_standards.text: Write simple interpretations of common texts in English supported with visual aids.
specific_standards.communication: Facilitate a discussion on a group project.

learning_outcomes: Can write a simple interpretation of common texts with visual aids (e.g., write 'recycle paper' and show a recycling symbol).

Can facilitate a group project discussion by writing prompts and showing visuals (e.g., 'Who wants to write the title of the project on the board?' and holds up a marker, helping the team decide who will take that role.).
Can use visual aids and simple phrases to clarify project instructions for peers (e.g., holds up a drawing of sorting bins and says, 'This is the blue bin for paper.').

recommended_grammatical_features: Future simple tense for plans (e.g., 'We will plant trees tomorrow.')
Imperatives for instructions (e.g., 'Bring a shovel to the park.')
Present simple to describe everyday events (e.g., 'We wash the plastic and glass bottles every day.')

pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness.pronunciation: Focus on the pronunciation of 'will' /wɪl/ and its contracted form (I'll) /aɪl/
pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness.phonemic_awareness: Segmenting multisyllabic words into syllables (e.g., 'presentation' into 'pre-sen-ta-tion')

pragmatic_competences: Give instructions and suggestions: 'Let's recycle paper.'
Explain how to recycle: 'Put paper in the blue bin.'
Describing everyday events: 'We usually sort the bottles by color and size.'
communicative_competences.sociolinguistic_competences: Discuss environmental actions in group discussions, such as proposing ways to reduce plastic waste.

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Classroom Recycling Campaign
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Students create a campaign promoting recycling. They will explain why recycling is essential, using the future with 'will' and imperative forms (e.g., 'Recycle paper and help protect the environment.' 'You will reduce waste by recycling.').

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Environmental Poster
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Students design posters explaining environmental actions. They will use the imperative form to suggest actions and explain what should be done to protect the environment (e.g., 'Save water.' 'Use reusable bags.' 'Turn off the lights when not in use.').

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Digital Recycling Instructions
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Students create digital instructions for recycling in their community. They will explain the steps, using simple present and imperative forms (e.g., 'Take plastic bottles to the recycling center.' 'Sort your waste into separate bins.' 'Recycling helps the community stay clean.').

skills: Environmental Awareness: Using the present simple tense to describe everyday events related to recycling.
Communication: Giving suggestions and creating instructions for community projects.
technology_integration: Use digital platforms for recycling instructions and campaign tools.

themes.theme_title: Today's Weather Will Be Sunny with Some Rain Later.
How Will the Weather Change Tomorrow?

listening.general_standard: Can identify general information and specific details heard from short oral texts when spoken slowly and clearly.

specific_standards.receptive: Identify specific details in spoken announcements.
specific_standards.interactive: Follow the thread of a conversation in role-plays.

learning_outcomes: Can identify details in spoken weather announcements (e.g., 'There will be rain tomorrow.').
Can recognize project-related spoken instructions for activities (e.g., 'Bring your materials tomorrow.').
Can follow the thread of conversations in role-plays about the weather (e.g., 'What's the weather like today?').

reading.general_standard: Can interpret information in fictional and factual short texts using basic reading strategies such as skimming, scanning and making inferences.

specific_standards.reading_1: Interpret simple charts and graphs related to texts.
specific_standards.reading_2: Write responses to questions about informational texts.
specific_standards.phonemic_awareness: Demonstrate knowledge of phonemic awareness by segmenting multisyllabic words into syllables.

learning_outcomes: Can interpret data about weather patterns in charts (e.g., 'More people like sunny days.').
Can answer questions about weather-related texts (e.g., 'What's the weather like tomorrow?' 'It will rain tomorrow.').
Can segment multisyllabic words into syllables, demonstrating knowledge of phonemic awareness (e.g., 'thermostat' into 'ther-mo-stat').

speaking.general_standard: Can exchange information about a variety of familiar topics read and discussed in class.

specific_standards.productive: Present findings from a simple survey supported with visual material.
specific_standards.interactive: Discuss plans for a trip.

learning_outcomes: Can present weather survey results with visual support (e.g., 'Most students like sunny days for outdoor activities.').
Can ask and clarify directions for outdoor activities (e.g., 'How is the weather today for going outside?').
Can discuss trip plans with classmates, based on the weather report (e.g., 'Let's visit the park when it is sunny.').

writing.general_standard: Can create simple texts in various genres, such as narratives, plans, and descriptions, incorporating details and peer feedback to improve clarity.

specific_standards.productive: Create instructions for using a tool or device.
specific_standards.interactive: Respond to peer writing.

learning_outcomes: Can write instructions for using a weather app (e.g., 'Open the app and check the temperature.').
Can list items to bring, based on weather predictions (e.g., 'Bring sunscreen and water if it's sunny.').
Can respond to peer comments on trip plans (e.g., 'It is a good idea to bring umbrellas in case it rains.').

mediation.general_standard: Can use strategies such as simplifying instructions, explaining main ideas, and using visuals or examples to negotiate meanings with peers.

specific_standards.communication: Confirm comprehension of peer contributions during discussions.
specific_standards.concept: Use diagrams to explain concepts to peers.

learning_outcomes: Can confirm understanding of peer contributions by writing keywords and showing visuals (e.g., write 'bring materials' and point to a list of supplies).
Can use diagrams to explain weather patterns to peers (e.g., draw a sun and clouds to show sunny and rainy weather).
Can summarize weather-related concepts for classmates by combining words and diagrams (e.g., write 'water cycle' next to a simple diagram).

recommended_grammatical_features: Future simple tense for weather predictions (e.g., 'It will be sunny tomorrow.')
Prepositions of place (e.g., 'The storm is over the lake.')
Modal verbs for recommendations (e.g., 'It looks like rain today; you should bring an umbrella.')

pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness.pronunciation: Practice intonation in weather predictions, emphasizing the last word of the sentence (e.g., 'It will be sunny.')
pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness.phonemic_awareness: Segmenting multisyllabic words into syllables (e.g., 'thermostat' into 'ther-mo-stat')

pragmatic_competences: Describe weather conditions: 'It will be sunny tomorrow.'
Ask about the forecast: 'What's the temperature tomorrow?'
Use prepositions of place: 'The rain is in the east.'
communicative_competences.sociolinguistic_competences: Engage in peer discussions on weather-related topics.

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Digital Weather Forecast Video
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Students create a digital weather forecast using the future tense and prepositions of place to describe weather changes.

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Weather Chart Creation
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Students create a weather chart, labeling weather changes with the future tense.

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Weather Report Presentation
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Students present a weather report using the future tense and weather vocabulary to the class.

skills: Weather Prediction: Describing weather changes in Panama and around the globe.
Communication: Describing weather with graphs and visuals.
technology_integration: Using video recording for forecasts and digital chart tools for weather charts.

themes.theme_title: Who Will Perform in the Fiestas Patrias Activities?
I Will Play the Drums in the Parade.

listening.general_standard: Can identify general information and specific details heard from short oral texts when spoken slowly and clearly.

specific_standards.receptive: Identify specific details in narratives that include expressions of feelings and attitudes.
specific_standards.interactive: Recognize the main ideas of the conversation when interacting in group discussions.

learning_outcomes: Can identify expressions of feelings and attitudes about participating in Fiestas Patrias celebrations (e.g., 'I'm proud to march in the parade.' 'I feel nervous about dancing in front of the whole school.').
Can recognize main ideas during group discussions about Fiestas Patrias preparations (e.g., 'Who will carry the Panamanian flag?' 'I will play the drums during the parade.').
Can understand specific details in conversations about parade roles and tasks (e.g., 'You need to wear your traditional uniform.' 'Don't forget to bring your instrument for the parade.').

reading.general_standard: Can interpret information in fictional and factual short texts using basic reading strategies such as skimming, scanning and making inferences.

specific_standards.reading_1: Create written reflections on stories read in class.
specific_standards.reading_2: Analyze characters' actions and motives in stories.
specific_standards.phonemic_awareness: Demonstrate knowledge of phonemic awareness by distinguishing spoken rhyming words from non-rhyming words.

learning_outcomes: Can write reflections on stories about Panamanian traditions and Fiestas Patrias (e.g., 'The girl felt proud wearing the traditional pollera dress in the parade.' 'The boy enjoyed playing the drums for the school band.').

Can analyze characters' actions and motives in stories about Fiestas Patrias celebrations (e.g., 'Liz practiced the traditional dance to perform in the parade.' 'Liz was chosen as the abanderada to lead the parade because she earned the top honor roll for being the best student in the class.').
Can distinguish rhyming words from non-rhyming words in simple comparisons (e.g., 'drum' and 'hum' vs. 'march' and 'flag').

speaking.general_standard: Can exchange information about a variety of familiar topics read and discussed in class.

specific_standards.productive: Present basic information about a hobby or interest.
specific_standards.interactive: Exchange directions.

learning_outcomes: Can present details of their performance to classmates (e.g., 'I will sing two songs in the Fiestas Patrias activities.' 'Liz is the Tambor Mayor. She enjoys leading the drummers in the parade, marking the rhythms, and keeping the group organized.').
Can ask for directions related to the talent show location (e.g., 'Where is the stage?').
Can provide basic information about their talent (e.g., 'I can play the drums in the parade.').

writing.general_standard: Can create simple texts in various genres, such as narratives, plans, and descriptions, incorporating details and peer feedback to improve clarity.

specific_standards.interactive: Edit short texts with peers.

learning_outcomes: Can write short descriptive paragraphs about preparing for Fiestas Patrias celebrations (e.g., 'If I practice the traditional dance every day, I will perform well in the parade.' 'I will wear my pollera during the school celebration.').

Can write coherent, simple descriptive texts about Fiestas Patrias events (e.g., 'First, the honor roll student will carry the Panamanian flag, then the school band will play, and finally, the dancers will perform traditional dances.').

Can edit and revise short descriptions of Fiestas Patrias activities with peers, adding details and suggestions (e.g., 'Let's add more information about the parade, like who will carry the Panamanian flag and what songs the band will play.').

mediation.general_standard: Can use strategies such as simplifying instructions, explaining main ideas, and using visuals or examples to negotiate meanings with peers.

specific_standards.communication: Relay complex information from teachers to students.
specific_standards.concept: Explain basic concepts using real-life examples.

learning_outcomes: Can explain basic concepts about Fiestas Patrias, using real-life examples and visuals (e.g., show a picture of students rehearsing a folkloric dance and write, 'Practice the dance steps.').

Can relay teacher instructions for Fiestas Patrias events by writing simple steps and using visuals (e.g., point to a clock drawing or a picture of the school gate and write, 'Meet at the school gate at 8 a.m.').
Can simplify parade preparation tasks using written steps and pictures (e.g., show an image of a student carrying the Panamanian flag in the parade and write, 'Hold the flag with both hands.').

recommended_grammatical_features: Future simple tense for plans (e.g., 'I will play the flute in the Panamanian National Holidays parade.')

First conditional (real possibility): Uses present simple in the 'if' clause + will in the main clause (e.g., 'If I practice the accordion every day, I will perform beautifully in the Panamanian National Holidays parade.')
Modal 'can' to express ability or talent (e.g., 'I can play the drums.')

pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness.pronunciation: Practice pronunciation of minimal pairs in short vowels (e.g., /ʌ/ in 'fun' and /æ/ in 'band').
pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness.phonemic_awareness: Distinguish spoken rhyming words from non-rhyming words related to Panama's National Holidays (e.g., 'drum' and 'hum' versus 'flag' and 'march').

pragmatic_competences: Share performance plans: 'I will perform first.'
Expressing facts and possibilities using conditionals: 'If you practice, you'll do great.'
Expressing ability and talents with the modal 'can': 'I can play the guitar.'
communicative_competences.sociolinguistic_competences: Use appropriate cultural expressions and formal language during Fiestas Patrias celebrations (e.g., '¡Viva Panamá!' during the parade or 'Congratulations on being the Abanderado!'). Collaborate respectfully with peers when planning Fiestas Patrias events, using polite language to assign tasks (e.g., 'Can you help carry the banner?' 'Let's decorate the classroom with Panamanian flags.').

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Fiestas Patrias Parade Planner
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Students plan a mock Fiestas Patrias parade, using the future simple tense to describe roles (e.g., 'I will carry the flag.'), and the first conditional for planning (e.g., 'If we practice, we will perform better.'). They will assign tasks, organize the parade sequence, and create a simple event schedule.

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Fiestas Patrias Celebration Documentary
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Students create a short documentary about Fiestas Patrias traditions, highlighting event preparations, cultural practices, and celebrations. The documentary will include interviews, performances, and key moments from the festivities.

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Fiestas Patrias Celebration Mural
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Students collaborate to create a mural showcasing key elements of Fiestas Patrias, including cultural symbols, traditional attire, and parade scenes. The mural will highlight Panamanian pride and the significance of the celebrations.

skills: Collaboration: Working effectively in teams to plan, create, and present projects, sharing responsibilities and ideas.
Creativity and Critical Thinking: Developing original ideas, problem-solving during project planning, and expressing cultural themes creatively.
Communication: Enhancing speaking, writing, and presentation skills to share information clearly and effectively across different formats.
technology_integration: Video Creation Tools: Utilize video recording and editing software to create documentaries and capture Fiestas Patrias's performances.
Digital Design Platforms: Use online design tools to create collaborative digital murals and visual materials highlighting cultural traditions.
